memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is his name. Pharaoh's chariots and his army he
has hurled into the sea. The best of Pharaoh's officers are drowned in the Red
Sea." - Ex 15:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"The LORD is a warrior." That is a description of God many of us handle
awkwardly. We are comfortable with God as shepherd, father, friend. Warrior sits
less easily.

But consider what it means here. God fought for a people who could not fight for
themselves. He took up arms against a nation that had drowned Hebrew babies in
the Nile and worked their parents to death. His warfare was on behalf of the
powerless.

A God who never opposed anything would not be loving. He would be indifferent.
Love that never gets angry at what destroys the beloved is not love at all.
Because God cares about the oppressed, He acts against oppression.

We should be careful with this, though. Israel did not fight this battle, and
the song is not a licence for God's people to take up violence in His name. They
stood still and watched. The warrior was God alone.

For believers, the New Testament is clear that "our struggle is not against flesh
and blood" (Eph 6:12). The enemies are sin, death, and the powers behind them.
And Christ has already fought that battle, disarming the powers and triumphing
over them at the cross (Col 2:15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you comfortable with a God who opposes evil?
2. What are you trying to fight that God has already defeated?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are a warrior who fights for the helpless. Thank You that at the cross
You defeated what I could never defeat. Amen.
